title: Dürer’s edge-unfolding conjecture
open: Prove that every convex polyhedron can be cut along a spanning tree of its edges and unfolded into one non-overlapping planar polygon, or construct a counterexample.
status: Commonly formalized through Shephard’s 1975 question; substantial special cases and affine-unfolding results do not settle the original conjecture.
why: Would clarify when rigid three-dimensional structures admit collision-free flat manufacturing layouts.
key_works: Ghomi (2014), *Affine unfoldings of convex polyhedra*, arXiv:1305.3231.

title: Sharp finite-budget guarantees for optimal sampling-based planning
open: Obtain practically useful, matching upper and lower bounds on samples needed to achieve a specified path-cost error, explicitly accounting for clearance, dimension, and obstacle geometry.
status: PRM* and RRT* established asymptotic optimality in 2011; asymptotic convergence alone does not provide this instance-sensitive stopping certificate.
why: Allows planners to report defensible quality-versus-computation guarantees.
key_works: Karaman and Frazzoli (2011), *Sampling-based Algorithms for Optimal Motion Planning*, arXiv:1105.1186.

title: Certifying infeasibility in narrow-passage problems
open: Develop practical planners that distinguish an undiscovered narrow passage from genuine infeasibility, with explicit geometric assumptions and independently checkable certificates.
status: Sampling planners can fail to find existing paths; exact geometric methods provide stronger conclusions but face scaling barriers. This is a tractability problem, not the absence of decidability results.
why: Prevents indefinite retries and false declarations that a manipulation task is impossible.
key_works: Orthey, Chamzas, and Kavraki (2024), *Sampling-Based Motion Planning: A Comparative Review*, arXiv:2309.13119.

title: Kinodynamic planning without a reliable steering function
open: Achieve strong completeness and convergence guarantees for high-dimensional nonlinear systems when connecting two states requires solving an unreliable numerical boundary-value problem.
status: Sampling and optimization methods cover important restricted dynamics; the difficult residual combines drift, unstable dynamics, state constraints, and bounded computation.
why: Extends dependable planning to agile aircraft, underactuated machines, and contact-rich systems.
key_works: Orthey, Chamzas, and Kavraki (2024), *Sampling-Based Motion Planning: A Comparative Review*, arXiv:2309.13119.

title: Planning across singular constraint manifolds
open: Construct planners that traverse changing-dimensional or singular configuration sets while maintaining constraint satisfaction and completeness guarantees.
status: Constraint-manifold sampling is established; transitions at kinematic singularities and changing contact constraints remain more demanding than planning on a smooth fixed manifold.
why: Supports closed-chain manipulation, coordinated carrying, and mechanism assembly.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2024/2025), *Motion Planning for Robotics: A Review for Sampling-based Planners*, arXiv:2410.19414.

title: Real-time global certificates for trajectory optimization
open: Produce globally valid optimality or bounded-suboptimality certificates for robot-scale nonlinear trajectories within an operational control deadline.
status: Semidefinite relaxation approaches provide certificates for structured polynomial problems; extending their tractable range remains open.
why: Replaces confidence in a local optimizer with auditable trajectory-quality guarantees.
key_works: Kang et al. (2024/2025), *Fast and Certifiable Trajectory Optimization*, arXiv:2406.05846.

title: Replanning guarantees under unpredictable obstacle motion
open: Characterize when a robot can preserve both safety and eventual task completion as obstacles move outside its prediction model, under explicit limits on their speed and behavior.
status: Dynamic planners and local avoidance methods exist; guarantees depend strongly on environmental assumptions and the availability of safe waiting or escape states.
why: Separates unavoidable deadlock from deficiencies of the planner.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2024/2025), *Motion Planning for Robotics: A Review for Sampling-based Planners*, arXiv:2410.19414.

title: Collision-query lower bounds for learned planners
open: Establish when learned geometric priors can provably reduce collision-checking complexity, and when distribution shift forces any planner back to worst-case exploration.
status: Learned sampling can accelerate favorable instances; the target is a matched information-theoretic account of its limits, not another favorable benchmark average.
why: Identifies which planning speedups can survive unfamiliar environments.
key_works: Karaman and Frazzoli (2011), *Sampling-based Algorithms for Optimal Motion Planning*, arXiv:1105.1186; Orthey et al. (2024), *Sampling-Based Motion Planning: A Comparative Review*.

title: Automatically discovering sound planning abstractions
open: Learn predicates and operators whose symbolic plans remain executable under continuous dynamics, including uncertainty and changes in object geometry.
status: Neuro-symbolic skill learning demonstrates useful abstractions; soundness and completeness across new task distributions remain stronger targets.
why: Removes extensive hand-written domain engineering without sacrificing executability.
key_works: Silver et al. (2023), *Learning Neuro-Symbolic Skills for Bilevel Planning*, arXiv:2206.10680.

title: Rearrangement planning with irreversible actions
open: Plan through clutter when moving, discarding, cutting, or fastening an object can permanently remove future options, while explicitly tracking recoverability.
status: Integrated task-and-motion planning handles many rearrangement domains; destructive actions and uncertain reversibility complicate standard search assumptions.
why: Enables repair, demolition, cooking, and assembly without premature irreversible mistakes.
key_works: Garrett et al. (2021), *Integrated Task and Motion Planning*, arXiv:2010.01083.

title: Belief-space task and motion planning at household scale
open: Jointly choose sensing, manipulation, and navigation actions while maintaining uncertainty over object existence, poses, affordances, and human intent.
status: Belief-space formulations and restricted demonstrations exist; large hybrid belief spaces remain a scaling obstacle.
why: Avoids treating uncertain scene interpretations as established facts.
key_works: Garrett et al. (2021), *Integrated Task and Motion Planning*, arXiv:2010.01083.

title: Planning with previously unknown tools
open: Infer the operational constraints of a novel tool through limited safe interaction, then incorporate it into a physically executable multistep plan.
status: Skill libraries support known tools and learned operators; discovering new tool semantics and their continuous constraints is a broader target.
why: Lets robots solve tasks outside a fixed catalog of end-effectors and fixtures.
key_works: Silver et al. (2023), *Learning Neuro-Symbolic Skills for Bilevel Planning*, arXiv:2206.10680.

title: Recovery-aware symbolic plans
open: Generate plans with executable contingency branches for slips, dropped objects, failed insertions, and changed human instructions, rather than assuming every action succeeds.
status: Task-and-motion frameworks integrate discrete and continuous feasibility; systematic recovery synthesis remains distinct from nominal plan generation.
why: Converts a successful demonstration into a usable autonomous workflow.
key_works: Garrett et al. (2021), *Integrated Task and Motion Planning*, arXiv:2010.01083.

title: Resource-aware concurrent manipulation
open: Plan overlapping robot actions while respecting temporary supports, shared tools, battery reserves, human access, and deadlines that depend on uncertain execution times.
status: PDDLStream links symbolic planning and continuous sampling; the proposed residual adds interacting temporal and physical resource constraints.
why: Supports useful parallel work rather than serialized toy workflows.
key_works: Garrett, Lozano-Pérez, and Kaelbling (2020), *PDDLStream: Integrating Symbolic Planners and Blackbox Samplers via Optimistic Adaptive Planning*, arXiv:1802.08705.

title: Calibrated black-box feasibility samplers
open: Make task planners reason correctly about samplers that sometimes fail despite feasible solutions, including learned grasp generators and numerical inverse-kinematics solvers.
status: Black-box streams provide a practical interface; distinguishing sampler inadequacy from physical infeasibility remains an important residual.
why: Prevents hidden numerical failures from corrupting high-level reasoning.
key_works: Garrett, Lozano-Pérez, and Kaelbling (2020), *PDDLStream*, arXiv:1802.08705.

title: Optimal allocation of symbolic and geometric search
open: Allocate finite computation among alternative symbolic plans, continuous parameter searches, sensing actions, and local optimization with performance guarantees.
status: Optimistic adaptive planning provides a concrete partial approach; universally effective allocation across heterogeneous search components is not established.
why: Avoids spending the entire planning budget refining an unproductive plan skeleton.
key_works: Garrett, Lozano-Pérez, and Kaelbling (2020), *PDDLStream*, arXiv:1802.08705.

title: Certifiable SLAM with unknown data association
open: Jointly infer landmark correspondences and robot trajectories with useful global certificates despite ambiguous appearances and outliers.
status: SE-Sync certifies structured synchronization problems; certification with unknown correspondences is substantially harder than optimizing a correctly associated graph.
why: Prevents confidently wrong maps caused by perceptual aliasing.
key_works: Rosen et al. (2019), *SE-Sync: A Certifiably Correct Algorithm for Synchronization over the Special Euclidean Group*, arXiv:1612.07386.

title: Place recognition under simultaneous appearance and structural change
open: Recognize previously visited places despite seasonal change, altered layouts, viewpoint shifts, and repeated architectural patterns, while reliably rejecting unseen places.
status: Contemporary place-recognition research covers multiple changes individually; their conjunction and calibrated rejection remain demanding.
why: Enables reliable return visits over months and years.
key_works: Yin et al. (2025), *General Place Recognition Survey: Towards Real-World Autonomy*, arXiv:2405.04812.

title: Persistent identity in dynamic maps
open: Maintain identities of objects that move, disappear, return, split into parts, or become occluded, without confusing temporary absence with permanent environmental change.
status: The robust-perception SLAM agenda explicitly extends beyond static geometry; persistent object identity requires additional temporal semantics.
why: Supports locating possessions, tracking maintenance, and reasoning about changes.
key_works: Cadena et al. (2016), *Past, Present, and Future of Simultaneous Localization and Mapping: Toward the Robust-Perception Age*, DOI:10.1109/TRO.2016.2624754.

title: Semantic-map uncertainty that remains calibrated
open: Represent uncertainty in semantic labels, geometry, and object relationships jointly, including correlations introduced by shared learned perception models.
status: Semantic mapping is established; treating neural confidence scores as calibrated map probabilities remains unjustified without additional modeling.
why: Makes downstream risk-sensitive planning meaningful.
key_works: Cadena et al. (2016), *Past, Present, and Future of Simultaneous Localization and Mapping*, DOI:10.1109/TRO.2016.2624754.

title: Bounded-memory lifelong mapping without catastrophic forgetting
open: Compress a continually changing map under a fixed memory budget while preserving information needed for future localization, navigation, and change detection.
status: Lifelong autonomy motivates map maintenance and forgetting; task-aware retention with quantified future performance is the sharper target.
why: Prevents map storage and maintenance costs from growing indefinitely.
key_works: Kunze et al. (2018), *Artificial Intelligence for Long-Term Robot Autonomy: A Survey*, arXiv:1807.05196.

title: Active SLAM with truthful information gain
open: Select exploration actions using information-gain estimates that remain accurate when future measurements are correlated, association is uncertain, and the observation model is learned.
status: Active SLAM has mature formulations; tractable approximations can change which exploration action appears most valuable.
why: Avoids expensive exploration that reduces an internal uncertainty metric without improving real knowledge.
key_works: Placed et al. (2023), *A Survey on Active Simultaneous Localization and Mapping: State of the Art and New Frontiers*, arXiv:2207.00254.

title: Consistent distributed SLAM with unknown correlations
open: Fuse maps from intermittently communicating robots without double-counting shared information, even when their processing histories and learned features overlap.
status: Distributed estimation offers conservative fusion strategies; efficient, informative fusion with uncertain dependencies remains difficult.
why: Enables collaborative mapping without artificial overconfidence.
key_works: Placed et al. (2023), *A Survey on Active Simultaneous Localization and Mapping*, arXiv:2207.00254.

title: Registration certificates under structured adversarial outliers
open: Determine practical identifiability and certification thresholds when incorrect correspondences form coherent competing alignments rather than independent random outliers.
status: TEASER demonstrates extreme outlier robustness in tested settings; structured ambiguity requires stronger assumptions than an outlier percentage alone.
why: Clarifies when apparently robust registration can still select the wrong physical alignment.
key_works: Yang, Shi, and Carlone (2021), *TEASER: Fast and Certifiable Point Cloud Registration*, arXiv:2001.07715.

title: Transparent-object geometry under uncontrolled illumination
open: Recover manipulation-relevant shape and uncertainty for transparent, refractive, and partially liquid-filled objects under unfamiliar backgrounds and lighting.
status: ClearGrasp demonstrated learned transparent-object reconstruction; reliable generalization beyond its training and sensing assumptions is a broader target.
why: Makes glassware, packaging, and laboratory manipulation dependable.
key_works: Sajjan et al. (2020), *ClearGrasp: 3D Shape Estimation of Transparent Objects for Manipulation*, arXiv:1910.02550.

title: Event-camera calibration during operation
open: Estimate changing event thresholds, timing offsets, temperature effects, and motion jointly without interrupting operation for laboratory calibration.
status: Event-based vision provides low-latency sensing; its measurement model and calibration differ materially from ordinary frame cameras.
why: Preserves reliable perception during high-speed and high-dynamic-range operation.
key_works: Gallego et al. (2022), *Event-based Vision: A Survey*, arXiv:1904.08405.

title: Tenfold lower-energy event-based perception
open: Proposed target: reduce total sensing-plus-computation energy by at least 10× against a matched frame-based pipeline while preserving specified detection latency and navigation reliability.
status: Event sensors offer sparse measurements; system-level savings must include preprocessing, idle power, and downstream inference.
why: Could extend the endurance of small autonomous robots.
key_works: Gallego et al. (2022), *Event-based Vision: A Survey*, arXiv:1904.08405.

title: Identifiable tactile force reconstruction
open: Determine when distributed contact forces and frictional stresses can be uniquely recovered from tactile images, including sensor hysteresis and unknown object compliance.
status: GelSight measures detailed contact geometry and supports force estimation; universal inversion requires resolving mechanical ambiguities.
why: Enables force-sensitive manipulation without relying solely on wrist measurements.
key_works: Yuan, Dong, and Adelson (2017), *GelSight: High-Resolution Robot Tactile Sensors for Estimating Geometry and Force*, DOI:10.3390/s17122762.

title: Tactile sensing that survives wear and contamination
open: Maintain calibrated tactile performance through abrasion, punctures, oil, dust, cleaning, and replacement of sensing skins.
status: High-resolution optical tactile sensors demonstrate rich measurements; lifetime stability is a separate deployment requirement.
why: Prevents dexterous policies from degrading as their contact surfaces age.
key_works: Yuan, Dong, and Adelson (2017), *GelSight*, DOI:10.3390/s17122762.

title: Multiple-source chemical localization in turbulent air
open: Infer the number, positions, and emission rates of changing chemical sources using moving, cross-sensitive sensors in unknown turbulent flow.
status: Gas-source localization has been studied since the 1990s; source mixtures, sensor memory, and uncontrolled flow remain central difficulties.
why: Supports leak detection and environmental monitoring without exposing people.
key_works: Francis et al. (2022), *Gas source localization and mapping with mobile robots: A review*, DOI:10.1002/rob.22109.

title: Open-set audition during robot motion
open: Remove motor, impact, and structural noise while preserving unfamiliar environmental sounds that were not enumerated during training.
status: A September 2026 preprint addresses open-set ego-noise separation; cross-platform transfer and preservation of rare safety-relevant sounds remain stronger evaluation targets.
why: Allows robots to hear people, failures, and events outside their visual field.
key_works: Shoda et al. (2026), *Open-Set Ego-Noise Separation for Legged-Robot Audition via Annotation-Free Adaptation and Pretrained-Model Transfer*, arXiv:2609.07440.

title: Active sensor placement without disturbing the phenomenon
open: Plan measurements that account for the robot’s own airflow, heat, vibration, illumination, and contact changing what it is trying to measure.
status: Mobile chemical sensing explicitly encounters platform-induced measurement effects; correcting them jointly with exploration remains challenging.
why: Makes robotic environmental measurements scientifically interpretable.
key_works: Francis et al. (2022), *Gas source localization and mapping with mobile robots: A review*, DOI:10.1002/rob.22109.

title: Physical resolution of the Painlevé paradox
open: Establish experimentally validated rules selecting physical outcomes when rigid-body Coulomb-friction models predict inconsistent or nonunique motion, especially in three-dimensional multicontact systems.
status: The paradox dates to the nineteenth century; compliance-based analyses clarify important cases without supplying a universal selection rule.
why: Determines whether simulated contact behavior represents a real robot–environment interaction.
key_works: Champneys and Várkonyi (2016), *The Painleve paradox in contact mechanics*, arXiv:1601.03545.

title: Simultaneous-impact laws for many contacts
open: Predict post-impact motion when several contacts occur nearly simultaneously, with experimentally identifiable parameters and controlled sensitivity to microscopic timing.
status: Different impact and time-stepping formulations can produce different outcomes; model selection requires more than numerical stability.
why: Improves predictions for falls, grasp closure, bouncing objects, and legged landing.
key_works: Le Lidec et al. (2024), *Contact Models in Robotics: a Comparative Analysis*, arXiv:2304.06372.

title: Friction models with history, wear, and contamination
open: Identify compact friction models that predict transitions among sticking, sliding, and rolling as surface state evolves during use.
status: Coulomb-style models remain useful approximations; contact-model comparisons expose consequential modeling choices.
why: Supports reliable manipulation beyond freshly calibrated laboratory surfaces.
key_works: Le Lidec et al. (2024), *Contact Models in Robotics: a Comparative Analysis*, arXiv:2304.06372.

title: Correct gradients through contact-mode changes
open: Obtain useful, mathematically justified sensitivities when trajectories create or break contacts, without gradients that optimize artifacts of a smoothing parameter.
status: Randomized smoothing and differentiable contact methods provide partial approaches; fidelity at nonsmooth transitions remains a central issue.
why: Makes gradient-based policy and mechanism optimization physically meaningful.
key_works: Le Lidec et al. (2021), *Leveraging randomized smoothing for optimal control of nonsmooth dynamical systems*; Montaut et al. (2023), *Differentiable Collision Detection: a Randomized Smoothing Approach*.

title: Quantifying simulator-induced policy bias
open: Bound how changing contact solvers, regularization, or friction approximations changes the policy selected by learning—not merely the simulated trajectory error.
status: Comparative contact studies show that modeling decisions matter; policy-level transfer guarantees require an additional theory.
why: Prevents agents from exploiting simulator-specific contact artifacts.
key_works: Le Lidec et al. (2024), *Contact Models in Robotics: a Comparative Analysis*, arXiv:2304.06372.

title: Contact-rich simulation at industrial particle counts
open: Simulate granular material, cables, cloth, and rigid tools together with validated force predictions at speeds useful for planning and learning.
status: Deformable-object simulators cover selected material classes; coupled heterogeneous contacts create additional accuracy and scaling demands.
why: Enables excavation, recycling, food handling, and bulk-material automation.
key_works: Lin et al. (2020), *SoftGym: Benchmarking Deep Reinforcement Learning for Deformable Object Manipulation*, arXiv:2011.07215.

title: Convergent rigid limits of compliant contact
open: Characterize when increasingly stiff compliant models converge to a unique rigid-contact trajectory and when different damping or regularization choices select different limits.
status: Painlevé-type behavior shows that the rigid limit can be singular; a broad classification for robot-relevant multicontact systems remains open.
why: Determines whether increasing simulator stiffness actually improves physical fidelity.
key_works: Champneys and Várkonyi (2016), *The Painleve paradox in contact mechanics*, arXiv:1601.03545.

title: Tenfold faster certified collision detection
open: Proposed target: achieve at least 10× lower end-to-end collision-checking cost on a public, difficult geometry suite while preserving conservative guarantees and matched hardware.
status: GJK++ accelerates established collision-detection machinery; a broad certified system-level target must include preprocessing and worst-case behavior.
why: Frees computation for larger searches and shorter control cycles.
key_works: Montaut et al. (2024), *GJK++: Leveraging Acceleration Methods for Faster Collision Detection*.

title: Fragility-aware grasping of unknown objects
open: Select and execute grasps while inferring unknown fracture, crushing, and surface-damage thresholds without using damaging trials.
status: General grasping and manipulation have advanced; unknown fragility introduces a separate hidden-state and safe-exploration problem.
why: Enables handling of produce, antiques, electronics, and thin packaging.
key_works: Billard and Kragic (2019), *Trends and challenges in robot manipulation*, DOI:10.1126/science.aat8414.

title: In-hand manipulation across unfamiliar object families
open: Reorient and reposition previously unseen objects with one hand despite unfamiliar mass distributions, friction, compliance, and contact geometry.
status: Learned dexterous in-hand manipulation demonstrated important sim-to-real results; object-family breadth and recovery remain stronger targets.
why: Reduces dependence on fixtures, regrasp stations, and specialized tooling.
key_works: OpenAI et al. (2018/2020), *Learning Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation*, arXiv:1808.00177.

title: Predicting slip before irreversible grasp loss
open: Detect incipient slip early enough to intervene across changing contact materials, without excessive grip force or sensor-specific retraining.
status: Tactile sensing exposes local deformation; transferring early-warning rules across contacts remains distinct from detecting an already slipping object.
why: Prevents drops while limiting damage and energy use.
key_works: Li et al. (2025), *The Developments and Challenges towards Dexterous and Embodied Robotic Manipulation: A Survey*, arXiv:2507.11840.

title: Manipulation through prolonged visual occlusion
open: Complete contact-rich operations using touch and proprioception when the hand, tool, or container blocks vision for an extended interval.
status: Dexterous systems integrate multiple sensing modalities; reliable state tracking through long occlusions remains a demanding residual.
why: Supports reaching into bags, assembling inside housings, and operating under furniture.
key_works: Li et al. (2025), *The Developments and Challenges towards Dexterous and Embodied Robotic Manipulation: A Survey*, arXiv:2507.11840.

title: General-purpose extrinsic dexterity
open: Discover how to use tables, walls, edges, gravity, and temporary supports to manipulate objects beyond the hand’s intrinsic capabilities.
status: Environmental contacts can extend manipulation capability; planning their use under uncertain friction and geometry remains difficult.
why: Could make simpler, cheaper hands substantially more capable.
key_works: Billard and Kragic (2019), *Trends and challenges in robot manipulation*, DOI:10.1126/science.aat8414.

title: Tool-use transfer across handle and working-end changes
open: Transfer a tool skill when the handle, functional tip, leverage, and required contact forces all differ from training examples.
status: General manipulation policies learn useful task families; identifying the causal role of each tool geometry remains an open generalization target.
why: Avoids retraining for every screwdriver, brush, utensil, or scraper.
key_works: Chi et al. (2023), *Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion*, arXiv:2303.04137.

title: Bimanual coordination under asymmetric uncertainty
open: Coordinate two hands when one has poor visibility or sensing, including load transfer, handoffs, and unexpected motion of the shared object.
status: ALOHA demonstrates fine-grained learned bimanual tasks; robust coordination under asymmetric failures requires additional mechanisms.
why: Enables large-object handling and delicate operations that cannot be decomposed into independent arm motions.
key_works: Zhao et al. (2023), *Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware*, arXiv:2304.13705.

title: Mobile manipulation without hidden environmental preparation
open: Complete household workflows across rooms without prepositioned objects, cleared approaches, fixed furniture poses, or human resets between subtasks.
status: Mobile ALOHA demonstrates learned whole-body mobile manipulation; removing preparation and reset assumptions is a stronger deployment target.
why: Measures useful autonomy rather than performance on carefully staged episodes.
key_works: Fu, Zhao, and Finn (2024), *Mobile ALOHA: Learning Bimanual Mobile Manipulation with Low-Cost Whole-Body Teleoperation*, arXiv:2401.02117.

title: Recovering hidden cloth topology
open: Infer folds, layers, openings, and self-contact from partial observations well enough to distinguish visually similar but operationally different cloth states.
status: Deformable-object research identifies occlusion and state representation as persistent challenges; visible surface reconstruction alone is insufficient.
why: Supports dressing, laundry, bedding, and fabric manufacturing.
key_works: Zhu et al. (2022), *Challenges and Outlook in Robotic Manipulation of Deformable Objects*, arXiv:2105.01767.

title: Reliable single-layer separation
open: Pick exactly one layer from stacked or folded textiles despite adhesion, static charge, porosity, and uncertain thickness.
status: Cloth manipulation has many successful task-specific systems; detecting accidental multilayer pickup and recovering reliably remains a distinct problem.
why: Enables garment production, laundry sorting, and sterile textile handling.
key_works: Zhu et al. (2022), *Challenges and Outlook in Robotic Manipulation of Deformable Objects*, arXiv:2105.01767.

title: Knot and tangle manipulation with hidden crossings
open: Identify and untangle previously unseen cable or rope configurations when crossings and endpoints are partially hidden, without tightening the knot or damaging the material.
status: Cable manipulation has specialized methods; topology changes, occlusion, and tension constraints require joint reasoning.
why: Supports household cables, surgical sutures, fishing gear, and industrial wiring.
key_works: McKenna and Oyekan (2026), *A Perspective on Open Challenges in Deformable Object Manipulation*, arXiv:2602.22998.

title: Cable routing with connector and bend constraints
open: Route flexible cables through clips and confined passages while satisfying bend radius, twist, tension, connector orientation, and serviceability requirements.
status: Deformable-object methods address individual routing operations; complete harness installation combines deformation, discrete ordering, and contact uncertainty.
why: Automates labor-intensive electronics and vehicle assembly.
key_works: McKenna and Oyekan (2026), *A Perspective on Open Challenges in Deformable Object Manipulation*, arXiv:2602.22998.

title: Cutting unknown heterogeneous materials
open: Adapt cutting trajectories and forces to hidden inclusions, anisotropy, and changing fracture behavior while meeting shape and damage constraints.
status: RoboNinja demonstrates adaptive cutting of multimaterial objects; wider material classes and calibrated failure prediction remain open.
why: Supports food preparation, recycling, manufacturing, and surgery.
key_works: Xu et al. (2023), *RoboNinja: Learning an Adaptive Cutting Policy for Multi-Material Objects*, arXiv:2302.11553.

title: Online rheology identification during manipulation
open: Infer task-relevant viscoelastic, plastic, and granular properties while manipulating a material, then adapt control without a separate characterization experiment.
status: Deformable-object control uses learned or fitted models; jointly identifying history-dependent constitutive behavior remains difficult.
why: Makes dough, gels, biological tissue, and soft packaging tractable.
key_works: Zhu et al. (2022), *Challenges and Outlook in Robotic Manipulation of Deformable Objects*, arXiv:2105.01767.

title: Dynamic cloth manipulation with predictable landing states
open: Fling, shake, or toss unfamiliar textiles so that their final folds and poses fall within specified tolerances, rather than merely increasing visible coverage.
status: FlingBot demonstrates effective dynamic unfolding; precise final-state control across fabrics is a stronger target.
why: Could dramatically shorten laundry and fabric-handling cycles.
key_works: Ha and Song (2022), *FlingBot: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Dynamic Manipulation for Cloth Unfolding*, arXiv:2105.03655.

title: Cross-material deformable-manipulation benchmarks
open: Build benchmarks with measured material properties, hidden-state ground truth, damage outcomes, and held-out materials, rather than only simulator-specific task success.
status: SoftGym supplies a useful simulation benchmark; physical cross-material transfer and standardized damage measurement require additional infrastructure.
why: Reveals whether progress reflects transferable manipulation or exploitation of one simulator.
key_works: Lin et al. (2020), *SoftGym*, arXiv:2011.07215.

title: Sim-to-real transfer under unmodeled physics
open: Transfer policies when reality contains contact, latency, deformation, or sensing mechanisms absent from the simulator—not merely different parameter values.
status: Domain randomization enabled dexterous transfer; expanding a parameter distribution cannot represent every structural model error.
why: Identifies when simulation training can be trusted.
key_works: OpenAI et al. (2018/2020), *Learning Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation*, arXiv:1808.00177.

title: Cross-embodiment learning without destructive averaging
open: Learn shared skills across robots with different kinematics, sensors, action interfaces, and capabilities while preserving embodiment-specific constraints.
status: Open X-Embodiment demonstrates benefits from pooled robot data; universal action semantics and reliable transfer remain broader targets.
why: Allows experience from one robot to improve others.
key_works: Open X-Embodiment Collaboration et al. (2023), *Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models*, arXiv:2310.08864.

title: Tenfold less real-robot data for new tasks
open: Proposed target: achieve matched held-out task success using at least 10× fewer real demonstrations and interventions, counting unsuccessful collection attempts.
status: Generalist policies and efficient demonstration interfaces provide baselines; a fair target must count all physical data and human assistance.
why: Makes adaptation affordable outside well-resourced laboratories.
key_works: Octo Model Team et al. (2024), *Octo: An Open-Source Generalist Robot Policy*, arXiv:2405.12213; Chi et al. (2024), *Universal Manipulation Interface*, arXiv:2402.10329.

title: Offline robot learning with hidden confounding
open: Learn valid action consequences from demonstrations when expert choices depend on unrecorded tactile cues, intentions, or environmental information.
status: Large datasets improve coverage, but observational trajectories alone do not automatically identify causal effects.
why: Prevents policies from copying correlations that fail when they choose different actions.
key_works: Khazatsky et al. (2024), *DROID: A Large-Scale In-The-Wild Robot Manipulation Dataset*, arXiv:2403.12945.

title: Autonomous learning without human resets
open: Let robots acquire skills while restoring usable training states themselves, including recovery from dropped, misplaced, or damaged objects.
status: Many learning setups separate task execution from reset; reset-free operation changes exploration, safety, and data accounting.
why: Removes a major hidden labor requirement from autonomous learning.
key_works: Brunke et al. (2022), *Safe Learning in Robotics: From Learning-Based Control to Safe Reinforcement Learning*, arXiv:2108.06266.

title: Continual skill acquisition without regression
open: Add new physical skills while preserving old capabilities, with evaluation that detects rare but consequential regressions after each update.
status: LIBERO benchmarks lifelong transfer; dependable retention across changing real-world tasks remains a larger target.
why: Prevents a useful robot from becoming less reliable as it learns.
key_works: Liu et al. (2023), *LIBERO: Benchmarking Knowledge Transfer for Lifelong Robot Learning*, arXiv:2306.03310.

title: Active collection of the most valuable robot experience
open: Choose demonstrations and autonomous trials that maximize future deployment improvement per unit of total cost, including operator time, wear, and failure risk.
status: Diverse datasets broaden experience; principled acquisition under these coupled physical costs is a separate optimization problem.
why: Directs expensive experiments toward the failures that matter.
key_works: Khazatsky et al. (2024), *DROID*, arXiv:2403.12945.

title: Representations invariant to irrelevant scene changes
open: Learn action representations that ignore background, lighting, and incidental objects while retaining subtle task-relevant differences such as contact state or a latch position.
status: Visuomotor policies demonstrate broad practical gains; invariance and sensitivity must be balanced rather than maximized independently.
why: Reduces brittle failures caused by visually unfamiliar but physically equivalent scenes.
key_works: Chi et al. (2023), *Diffusion Policy*, arXiv:2303.04137.

title: Grounding underspecified instructions in physical affordances
open: Resolve instructions such as “put this away safely” using the actual scene, user constraints, and robot capabilities, while asking only necessary clarifying questions.
status: SayCan grounds language in skill affordances; ambiguous goals and unmodeled constraints require richer grounding.
why: Makes natural-language control useful beyond curated commands.
key_works: Ahn et al. (2022), *Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances*, arXiv:2204.01691.

title: Calibrated confidence for vision–language–action policies
open: Predict whether a proposed action sequence will succeed or cause harm under deployment shift, with calibration measured on physical outcomes.
status: OpenVLA provides an open generalist policy; generative likelihood is not itself a calibrated task-success probability.
why: Supports justified abstention, human assistance, and risk-sensitive execution.
key_works: Kim et al. (2024), *OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model*, arXiv:2406.09246.

title: Compositional transfer of physical skills
open: Execute new combinations of familiar objects, relations, and skills without requiring demonstrations of each combination.
status: RT-2 transfers web-derived knowledge into robotic control; systematic compositional generalization is stronger than success on selected novel instructions.
why: Prevents data requirements from growing combinatorially with task combinations.
key_works: Brohan et al. (2023), *RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control*, arXiv:2307.15818.

title: Progress recognition without visual reward shortcuts
open: Determine whether a task is genuinely progressing or complete when appearances can be misleading—for example, a closed drawer that still obstructs an object.
status: Language-conditioned spatial representations enable useful task specification; physical completion verification remains an additional requirement.
why: Prevents false success reports and repeated ineffective actions.
key_works: Huang et al. (2023), *VoxPoser: Composable 3D Value Maps for Robotic Manipulation with Language Models*, arXiv:2307.05973.

title: Counterfactual physical reasoning before action
open: Predict the consequences of alternative actions well enough to reject plausible but physically invalid plans involving support, containment, force, or irreversible changes.
status: General robot control models demonstrate broad behavior; reliable counterfactual reasoning is not established merely by producing fluent plans.
why: Reduces mistakes that cannot be repaired after execution.
key_works: Black et al. (2024/2025), *π0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control*, arXiv:2410.24164.

title: Verifiable language-generated robot programs
open: Translate instructions into executable programs with checked preconditions, resource bounds, authority limits, and safe behavior when perception is wrong.
status: Code as Policies demonstrates language-generated control code; full physical and authorization contracts require additional verification.
why: Prevents generated programs from bypassing safety through valid-looking API calls.
key_works: Liang et al. (2022), *Code as Policies: Language Model Programs for Embodied Control*, arXiv:2209.07753.

title: Reward synthesis that resists exploitation
open: Generate robot-training objectives that preserve intended behavior under optimization, including costs omitted from demonstrations such as damage, nuisance, and unsafe shortcuts.
status: Eureka demonstrates effective automated reward design; optimization-resistant specification remains a stronger requirement.
why: Avoids producing impressive but operationally unacceptable policies.
key_works: Ma et al. (2023), *Eureka: Human-Level Reward Design via Coding Large Language Models*, arXiv:2310.12931.

title: Long-horizon execution in genuinely unfamiliar homes
open: Complete extended household workflows with recoveries, changing occupants, and unfamiliar object organization, evaluated without per-home tuning.
status: π0.5 reports open-world generalization, including unfamiliar homes; sustained reliability and recovery exceed one successful generalization demonstration.
why: Connects generalist-policy research to useful domestic autonomy.
key_works: Physical Intelligence et al. (2025), *π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization*, arXiv:2504.16054.

title: Weeks of useful work without unrecorded intervention
open: Demonstrate sustained operation with complete logs of repairs, resets, teleoperation, cleaning, charging assistance, and task exclusions.
status: Long-term autonomy has an established research history; transparent accounting of all supporting labor is essential to this stronger target.
why: Distinguishes genuine autonomy from a robot supported by an invisible operations team.
key_works: Kunze et al. (2018), *Artificial Intelligence for Long-Term Robot Autonomy: A Survey*, arXiv:1807.05196.

title: Distinguishing hardware faults from environmental novelty
open: Diagnose whether poor performance comes from wear, sensor failure, changed surroundings, or an inadequate policy, using only available operational evidence.
status: Long-term autonomy requires monitoring and adaptation; confounding among these failure causes remains difficult.
why: Prevents inappropriate repairs, unsafe continued operation, and unnecessary retraining.
key_works: Kunze et al. (2018), *Artificial Intelligence for Long-Term Robot Autonomy: A Survey*, arXiv:1807.05196.

title: Safe adaptation to previously unseen damage
open: Recover useful behavior after unanticipated damage without exploratory actions that worsen damage or endanger people.
status: Intelligent trial-and-error adaptation demonstrated rapid recovery from selected damage cases; unforeseen damage with strict safety constraints is a broader target.
why: Keeps remote or expensive robots useful after partial failures.
key_works: Cully et al. (2015), *Robots that can adapt like animals*, DOI:10.1038/nature14422; arXiv:1407.3501.

title: Self-recalibration after mechanical drift
open: Identify changes in joint offsets, compliance, sensor alignment, and actuation without external metrology or dangerous calibration motions.
status: Rapid adaptation methods infer latent dynamics during operation; full geometric and sensing recalibration requires additional observability.
why: Preserves accuracy as robots age or receive replacement parts.
key_works: Kumar et al. (2021), *RMA: Rapid Motor Adaptation for Legged Robots*, arXiv:2107.04034.

title: Autonomous physical self-repair
open: Diagnose a replaceable fault, obtain or manipulate a spare component, perform replacement, and verify restored capability without another robot or human doing the difficult steps.
status: Damage adaptation changes behavior rather than repairing hardware; this target adds physical restoration and verification.
why: Could fundamentally change remote-operation economics.
key_works: Cully et al. (2015), *Robots that can adapt like animals*, DOI:10.1038/nature14422.

title: Joint scheduling of work, charging, and degradation
open: Schedule missions and charging while accounting for uncertain future demand, battery aging, thermal limits, and the possibility of becoming unable to reach a charger.
status: Energy management is part of long-term autonomy; degradation-aware operation adds a long-horizon resource tradeoff.
why: Improves lifetime productivity rather than only today’s task count.
key_works: Kunze et al. (2018), *Artificial Intelligence for Long-Term Robot Autonomy: A Survey*, arXiv:1807.05196.

title: Useful autonomy through cloud and network outages
open: Preserve safe, coherent task execution when remote inference, maps, identity services, or fleet coordination become unavailable.
status: ROS 2 supports distributed robotic systems; application-level continuity across partial service failures remains a separate responsibility.
why: Prevents network availability from becoming a hidden safety assumption.
key_works: Macenski et al. (2022), *Robot Operating System 2: Design, Architecture, and Uses In The Wild*, arXiv:2211.07752.

title: Restart recovery without duplicate physical actions
open: After a controller restart, determine which actions physically occurred and resume without duplicate dispensing, cutting, fastening, or object transfer.
status: Formal robotic verification addresses system behavior; durable software state alone cannot reveal an unobserved physical effect.
why: Makes retries safe for irreversible actions.
key_works: Luckcuck et al. (2019), *Formal Specification and Verification of Autonomous Robotic Systems: A Survey*, arXiv:1807.00048.

title: End-to-end safety contracts that include perception
open: Prove useful safety properties when the controller’s state estimate comes from fallible learned perception, rather than assuming exact state or a fixed bounded error.
status: Safe-learning methods provide conditional guarantees; perception failures can violate the conditions on which those guarantees depend.
why: Closes a major gap between controller proofs and deployed systems.
key_works: Brunke et al. (2022), *Safe Learning in Robotics*, arXiv:2108.06266.

title: High-dimensional reachability without unsafe approximation
open: Compute useful reachable sets for high-dimensional robot dynamics while controlling approximation error and meeting real-time requirements.
status: Hamilton–Jacobi reachability gives strong guarantees for tractable state dimensions; dimensional scaling remains a central obstacle.
why: Enables principled collision avoidance and recoverability analysis.
key_works: Bansal et al. (2017), *Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability: A Brief Overview and Recent Advances*, arXiv:1709.07523.

title: Closed-loop conformal guarantees under adaptive distribution shift
open: Retain meaningful finite-sample risk guarantees when robot actions alter the data distribution and invalidate ordinary exchangeability assumptions.
status: Conformal methods are being integrated with verification and control; adaptive closed-loop deployment requires additional assumptions or new theory.
why: Makes statistical safety claims applicable to acting systems.
key_works: Lindemann et al. (2024), *Formal Verification and Control with Conformal Prediction*, arXiv:2409.00536.

title: Barrier functions across contact-mode transitions
open: Construct control barrier functions that remain valid through impact, sticking, sliding, and contact loss, including uncertain transition times.
status: Barrier-function theory provides powerful continuous-system tools; hybrid contact dynamics require additional compatibility conditions.
why: Extends safety filtering to dexterous and legged behavior.
key_works: Ames et al. (2019), *Control Barrier Functions: Theory and Applications*, arXiv:1903.11199.

title: Safe exploration when the safe set is initially unknown
open: Characterize how much an agent can learn while respecting safety constraints that themselves must be inferred from experience.
status: Safe reinforcement learning typically needs initial safe knowledge, conservative models, or recoverable regions; the necessity of these assumptions deserves sharper bounds.
why: Separates achievable autonomous learning from impossible guarantees.
key_works: Brunke et al. (2022), *Safe Learning in Robotics*, arXiv:2108.06266.

title: Verification of large learned policies in closed loop
open: Verify a robot’s learned perception–policy–dynamics composition over meaningful time horizons and operational regions, without reducing the specification to a trivial local property.
status: Formal methods verify restricted robotic components and systems; large neural and hybrid compositions create state-space and modeling barriers.
why: Produces evidence stronger than passing a finite collection of scenarios.
key_works: Luckcuck et al. (2019), *Formal Specification and Verification of Autonomous Robotic Systems*, arXiv:1807.00048.

title: Certifying online policy updates
open: Allow a robot to improve during deployment while ensuring that every accepted update preserves specified safety and essential capabilities.
status: Runtime assurance and barrier-based filtering provide partial protection; certifying an evolving complete behavior remains more demanding.
why: Reconciles continual learning with dependable operation.
key_works: Ames et al. (2019), *Control Barrier Functions: Theory and Applications*, arXiv:1903.11199; Luckcuck et al. (2019), *Formal Specification and Verification of Autonomous Robotic Systems*.

title: Composing risk across long missions
open: Allocate and update a mission-wide risk budget when failures are dependent, exposure changes over time, and task selection adapts to observations.
status: Per-action or per-trajectory guarantees do not automatically provide informative lifetime guarantees.
why: Prevents individually “safe” actions from accumulating unacceptable operational risk.
key_works: Lindemann et al. (2024), *Formal Verification and Control with Conformal Prediction*, arXiv:2409.00536.

title: Locomotion over visually deceptive terrain
open: Traverse surfaces whose appearance misrepresents support or traction, such as vegetation over holes, thin crusts, loose coverings, and transparent obstacles.
status: Perceptive locomotion systems demonstrate impressive outdoor robustness; hidden load-bearing properties remain a distinct uncertainty.
why: Extends legged mobility beyond terrain recognizable from images alone.
key_works: Miki et al. (2022), *Learning robust perceptive locomotion for quadrupedal robots in the wild*, arXiv:2201.08117.

title: Foothold selection with uncertain friction and compliance
open: Choose footholds and contact forces while simultaneously estimating whether each surface will slip, deform, or collapse under load.
status: Rapid adaptation handles changing dynamics; anticipating a previously untested foothold adds a prospective identification problem.
why: Reduces falls before the controller has enough evidence to adapt.
key_works: Kumar et al. (2021), *RMA: Rapid Motor Adaptation for Legged Robots*, arXiv:2107.04034.

title: Controlled falling and recovery in clutter
open: Select a fall trajectory that minimizes injury and damage, then recover from arbitrary reachable resting configurations without requiring clear surrounding space.
status: Agile locomotion has advanced substantially; ordinary locomotion benchmarks do not establish safe failure and recovery behavior.
why: Makes inevitable failures survivable in occupied environments.
key_works: Zhuang, Yao, and Zhao (2025), *Humanoid Parkour Learning*, PMLR 270:1975–1991.

title: Whole-body locomotion while manipulating uncertain loads
open: Coordinate stepping, balance, arm motion, and contact forces while a carried object’s mass or contents change unexpectedly.
status: Whole-body mobile manipulation and agile locomotion have separate strong demonstrations; their robust integration remains demanding.
why: Enables useful carrying and tool work rather than locomotion-only demonstrations.
key_works: Fu et al. (2024), *Mobile ALOHA*, arXiv:2401.02117; Zhuang et al. (2025), *Humanoid Parkour Learning*.

title: Agile locomotion with meaningful human-safety envelopes
open: Preserve useful speed and agility while enforcing impact, separation, and emergency-stop requirements around unpredictable people.
status: Parkour policies demonstrate complex traversal; human-compatible safety is a different objective from obstacle-course completion.
why: Determines whether agile robots can operate in ordinary shared spaces.
key_works: Rudin et al. (2026), *Parkour in the wild: Learning a general and extensible agile locomotion policy using multi-expert distillation and RL fine-tuning*, DOI:10.1177/02783649261455067.

title: Thermally sustainable locomotion policies
open: Optimize gait for long-duration useful work while respecting motor, gearbox, battery, and electronics temperatures rather than only instantaneous torque limits.
status: Rapidly trained locomotion policies demonstrate strong motor skills; thermal accumulation requires longer-horizon objectives and models.
why: Prevents short demonstrations from masking unsustainable duty cycles.
key_works: Rudin et al. (2021), *Learning to Walk in Minutes Using Massively Parallel Deep Reinforcement Learning*, arXiv:2109.11978.

title: Locomotion transfer across substantial morphology changes
open: Transfer gait competence across different leg lengths, mass distributions, joint arrangements, and actuator capabilities without extensive retraining.
status: Adaptation and domain randomization handle important variations; changes in controllability and feasible contact patterns require more than parameter tuning.
why: Reduces the training cost of new robot designs.
key_works: Kumar et al. (2021), *RMA*, arXiv:2107.04034; Rudin et al. (2021), *Learning to Walk in Minutes*, arXiv:2109.11978.

title: Field measurements of gait-induced wear
open: Establish how locomotion policies affect joint wear, foot degradation, fastener loosening, and maintenance intervals across real terrain and weather.
status: Outdoor and energy-efficient locomotion demonstrations provide baselines; standardized longitudinal wear comparisons are a separate experimental target.
why: Optimizes robot lifetime rather than only speed or benchmark success.
key_works: Badri-Spröwitz et al. (2022), *BirdBot achieves energy-efficient gait with minimal control using avian-inspired leg clutching*, DOI:10.1126/scirobotics.abg4055.

title: High-speed flight under unfamiliar gusts and visibility
open: Maintain collision avoidance at high speed when gusts, lighting, precipitation, and aerodynamic disturbances depart from training conditions.
status: High-speed wild flight and champion-level racing have been demonstrated; those achievements do not establish universal robustness to unfamiliar disturbances.
why: Enables reliable inspection and emergency response outside prepared courses.
key_works: Loquercio et al. (2021), *Learning High-Speed Flight in the Wild*, arXiv:2110.05113; Kaufmann et al. (2023), *Champion-level drone racing using deep reinforcement learning*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-06419-4.

title: Fully onboard grasping of unfamiliar moving targets
open: Grasp moving objects with unknown geometry and motion using onboard sensing and computation, without motion capture or prior object models.
status: Ubellacker et al. demonstrated onboard static-target grasps up to 2 m/s; their moving-target experiments used motion capture.
why: Supports dynamic pickup, emergency supply transfer, and aerial logistics.
key_works: Ubellacker et al. (2024), *High-speed aerial grasping using a soft drone with onboard perception*, DOI:10.1038/s44182-024-00012-1.

title: Rapid identification of payload-induced aerodynamics
open: Estimate and compensate for changes in inertia, drag, downwash blockage, and center of mass immediately after grasping an unfamiliar payload.
status: Adaptive aerial grasping compensates for added mass; broad payload geometry introduces additional coupled aerodynamic effects.
why: Prevents successful grasps from turning into unstable flight.
key_works: Ubellacker et al. (2024), *High-speed aerial grasping using a soft drone with onboard perception*, DOI:10.1038/s44182-024-00012-1.

title: Stable aerial force application on uncertain surfaces
open: Maintain prescribed contact forces during drilling, wiping, inspection, or fastening despite wind, surface compliance, and uncertain reaction forces.
status: Aerial manipulation prototypes demonstrate contact tasks; outdoor robustness and coupled force–flight control remain challenging.
why: Allows flying robots to perform maintenance rather than only observe.
key_works: Barakou, Tzafestas, and Valavanis (2024), *A Review of Real-Time Implementable Cooperative Aerial Manipulation Systems*, DOI:10.3390/drones8050196.

title: Cooperative aerial transport with delayed communication
open: Transport and precisely place shared loads despite communication delays, cable slack, wind, and failure of one aircraft.
status: Cooperative aerial manipulation has laboratory demonstrations; the review identifies outdoor disturbances and communication as continuing difficulties.
why: Enables transport of objects beyond one aircraft’s capacity.
key_works: Barakou et al. (2024), *A Review of Real-Time Implementable Cooperative Aerial Manipulation Systems*, DOI:10.3390/drones8050196.

title: Reliable perching and departure across surface classes
open: Approach, attach to, remain on, and depart from unfamiliar natural and engineered surfaces without a surface-specific attachment mechanism.
status: Spines, adhesives, and grippers each support subsets of surfaces; versatile attachment remains limited by material and geometry dependence.
why: Extends endurance and enables persistent observation.
key_works: *Current Status, Challenges, and Prospects for New Types of Aerial Robots* (2024), DOI:10.1016/j.eng.2024.05.008; author list **(verify)**.

title: Insect-scale untethered flight with useful autonomy
open: Integrate propulsion, energy, sensing, control, and communication into an insect-scale aircraft that performs useful tasks without external power or external state tracking.
status: Flapping-wing and miniature aerial systems advance individual components; integrated endurance and autonomy remain a coupled scaling problem.
why: Opens access to confined spaces and distributed environmental sensing.
key_works: *Current Status, Challenges, and Prospects for New Types of Aerial Robots* (2024), DOI:10.1016/j.eng.2024.05.008; author list **(verify)**.

title: Emergency landing after partial actuator failure
open: Identify a survivable landing strategy after propulsion or sensing failure while accounting for uncertain terrain and nearby people.
status: Agile flight research provides sophisticated nominal control; failure recovery requires different dynamics, objectives, and validation.
why: Determines whether aerial autonomy can fail safely.
key_works: Kaufmann et al. (2023), *Champion-level drone racing using deep reinforcement learning*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-06419-4.

title: Continuous-time multi-agent pathfinding with physical dynamics
open: Scale coordinated planning when robots have different shapes, accelerations, turning constraints, and uncertain execution times rather than identical grid moves.
status: MAPF has clear discrete formulations and benchmarks; realistic dynamics change both feasibility and computational structure.
why: Bridges algorithmic progress to actual fleets.
key_works: Stern et al. (2019), *Multi-Agent Pathfinding: Definitions, Variants, and Benchmarks*, arXiv:1906.08291.

title: Online fleet planning without starvation or gridlock
open: Handle continuous task arrivals, failed robots, blocked routes, and changing priorities while guaranteeing progress and bounded unfairness.
status: MAPF variants formalize many fleet-planning choices; lifelong arrival and disruption models require additional guarantees.
why: Prevents efficient average throughput from hiding indefinitely delayed jobs.
key_works: Stern et al. (2019), *Multi-Agent Pathfinding*, arXiv:1906.08291.

title: Heterogeneous task allocation with uncertain capabilities
open: Assign cooperative tasks when robot skills, health, availability, and task requirements are uncertain and evolve during execution.
status: Swarm engineering addresses coordination; heterogeneous capability learning and allocation are more demanding than homogeneous role assignment.
why: Makes mixed fleets resilient and economically useful.
key_works: Brambilla et al. (2013), *Swarm robotics: a review from the swarm engineering perspective*, DOI:10.1007/s11721-012-0075-2.

title: Synthesizing local rules with global guarantees
open: Derive decentralized robot rules from a desired collective behavior, with guarantees on convergence, robustness, and resource consumption.
status: Swarms can exhibit useful collective behavior; predictable engineering from specification remains a foundational challenge.
why: Replaces trial-and-error emergence with systematic design.
key_works: Brambilla et al. (2013), *Swarm robotics*, DOI:10.1007/s11721-012-0075-2; Dorigo, Théraulaz, and Trianni (2020), *Reflections on the future of swarm robotics*, DOI:10.1126/scirobotics.abe4385.

title: Byzantine-resilient physical swarms
open: Preserve specified collective functions when some robots provide false information or act inconsistently, without assuming a trusted central controller.
status: Swarm robustness to ordinary failures does not automatically imply resilience to strategically misleading participants.
why: Protects infrastructure-scale fleets against compromised or malfunctioning members.
key_works: Dorigo et al. (2020), *Reflections on the future of swarm robotics*, DOI:10.1126/scirobotics.abe4385.

title: Communication lower bounds for embodied coordination
open: Determine the minimum information exchange needed for specified collective tasks under limited sensing, occlusion, mobility, and intermittent connectivity.
status: Local-rule swarms demonstrate coordination without rich communication; tight task-dependent lower bounds remain a distinct theoretical target.
why: Guides radio, sensing, and control architecture choices.
key_works: Brambilla et al. (2013), *Swarm robotics*, DOI:10.1007/s11721-012-0075-2.

title: Three-dimensional self-assembly with load-bearing guarantees
open: Assemble and repair three-dimensional structures from mobile modules while maintaining mechanical stability throughout intermediate configurations.
status: Thousand-robot programmable self-assembly demonstrated large-scale planar shape formation; load-bearing three-dimensional construction adds mechanical constraints.
why: Enables adaptable structures and deployable infrastructure.
key_works: Rubenstein, Cornejo, and Nagpal (2014), *Programmable self-assembly in a thousand-robot swarm*, DOI:10.1126/science.1254295.

title: Reproducible swarm scaling in real environments
open: Measure how reliability, maintenance labor, communication, and useful throughput scale from tens to thousands of physical robots outside controlled arenas.
status: Large laboratory swarms establish feasibility at scale; field reliability and total support cost require separate longitudinal evidence.
why: Tests whether swarm advantages survive operational overhead.
key_works: Rubenstein et al. (2014), *Programmable self-assembly in a thousand-robot swarm*, DOI:10.1126/science.1254295.

title: Complete classification of mobile spatial 6R linkages
open: Classify spatial closed chains of six revolute joints that possess nontrivial mobility, including exceptional and degenerate families under clearly stated equivalences.
status: Bond theory and algebraic methods establish important families and necessary conditions; paradoxically mobile linkages remain a rich classification frontier.
why: Expands the catalog of compact mechanisms available for robotic design.
key_works: Schicho (2022), *And Yet It Moves: Paradoxically Moving Linkages in Kinematics*, arXiv:2004.12635; DOI:10.1090/bull/1721.

title: Tolerance-robust overconstrained mechanisms
open: Design useful overconstrained linkages whose mobility and load capacity survive realistic manufacturing errors, wear, and thermal distortion.
status: Exact algebraic mobility can depend on special geometric relations; robust realizability is a different question from ideal kinematic existence.
why: Converts elegant mechanism families into manufacturable robots.
key_works: Schicho (2022), *And Yet It Moves*, arXiv:2004.12635.

title: High-torque actuators with sustained thermal performance
open: Improve continuous torque density while preserving efficiency, backdrivability, impact tolerance, and acceptable temperature over realistic duty cycles.
status: Actuator architectures offer competing advantages; peak specifications do not settle sustained multi-objective performance.
why: Determines practical payload and endurance.
key_works: Vanderborght et al. (2013), *Variable impedance actuators: A review*, DOI:10.1016/j.robot.2013.06.009.

title: Wide-band variable impedance with guaranteed passivity
open: Achieve rapid, accurate stiffness and damping changes across a broad operating range without destabilizing contact or injecting uncontrolled energy.
status: Variable-impedance and elastic actuation are established; bandwidth, range, efficiency, and stability remain coupled tradeoffs.
why: Enables safe physical interaction without making robots slow or weak.
key_works: Vanderborght et al. (2013), *Variable impedance actuators: A review*, DOI:10.1016/j.robot.2013.06.009.

title: Tenfold longer-lived artificial muscles
open: Proposed target: increase useful actuation cycles by at least 10× at matched strain, stress, frequency, and packaging volume, including performance after partial damage.
status: HASEL actuators demonstrate muscle-like performance and electrical self-healing; mechanical lifetime under matched workloads is a separate target.
why: Could make soft actuation operationally competitive.
key_works: Acome et al. (2018), *Hydraulically amplified self-healing electrostatic actuators with muscle-like performance*, DOI:10.1126/science.aao6139.

title: Useful onboard power for small untethered robots
open: Integrate energy storage, conversion, cooling, and distribution without consuming the mass and volume needed for sensing and actuation.
status: Power remains one of the broad robotics challenges identified in 2018; component energy density alone does not determine usable system endurance.
why: Enables autonomous operation beyond tethered demonstrations.
key_works: Yang et al. (2018), *The grand challenges of Science Robotics*, DOI:10.1126/scirobotics.aar7650.

title: Co-design that optimizes lifetime usefulness
open: Jointly optimize body, actuator, controller, sensing, manufacturability, repairability, and lifetime performance rather than a narrow simulated task score.
status: Recent holistic co-design work explicitly identifies narrow objectives and simulation–reality gaps as limitations.
why: Avoids designs that excel in optimization but fail as usable machines.
key_works: Stölzle et al. (2025/2026), *Soft yet Effective Robots via Holistic Co-Design*, arXiv:2505.03761.

title: Mechanically and semantically interchangeable robot modules
open: Create replaceable actuator and sensor modules that automatically communicate calibration, limits, failure modes, and control semantics as well as electrical compatibility.
status: Modularity simplifies construction, but physical interchangeability does not itself preserve control behavior.
why: Reduces repair labor and platform-specific integration.
key_works: Vanderborght et al. (2013), *Variable impedance actuators: A review*, DOI:10.1016/j.robot.2013.06.009; Macenski et al. (2022), *Robot Operating System 2*, arXiv:2211.07752.

title: Observable state representations for continuum bodies
open: Recover enough of a soft robot’s distributed shape, strain, and internal pressure to control it reliably using a practical number of sensors.
status: Soft robots challenge finite-dimensional modeling; task-dependent reduced representations are useful but not universally sufficient.
why: Enables feedback control without instrumenting every part of the body.
key_works: Rus and Tolley (2015), *Design, fabrication and control of soft robots*, DOI:10.1038/nature14543.

title: Control through hysteresis and material aging
open: Maintain accurate soft-robot behavior as material response depends on loading history, temperature, and age, without frequent full retraining.
status: Soft-robot design and control accommodate nonlinear materials; long-term history-dependent changes remain a separate challenge.
why: Preserves repeatability in practical use.
key_works: Rus and Tolley (2015), *Design, fabrication and control of soft robots*, DOI:10.1038/nature14543.

title: Fully soft closed-loop autonomy
open: Build an entirely soft untethered robot that senses its environment, makes nontrivial decisions, and adapts its behavior without rigid electronic control components.
status: Octobot demonstrated integrated entirely soft autonomous operation; richer environmental feedback and programmable decision-making are stronger targets.
why: Expands robots that can safely deform through extreme confinement.
key_works: Wehner et al. (2016), *An integrated design and fabrication strategy for entirely soft, autonomous robots*, DOI:10.1038/nature19100.

title: Retraction of growing robots without buckling or entanglement
open: Retract a long deployed growing robot through tortuous passages while preserving steering, payload integrity, and environmental contact limits.
status: Growth-based navigation demonstrated a distinctive access mechanism; controlled reusable retraction adds different mechanical constraints.
why: Makes growing robots retrievable and reusable.
key_works: Hawkes et al. (2017), *A soft robot that navigates its environment through growth*, DOI:10.1126/scirobotics.aan3028.

title: Autonomous branching and tool delivery by growing robots
open: Grow through branching passages, select routes, and deliver useful tools while managing distributed friction, pressure, and material supply.
status: Tip-growth navigation is demonstrated; branching decisions and sustained tool operation require integrated planning and mechanics.
why: Enables pipe inspection, confined-space repair, and minimally invasive access.
key_works: Hawkes et al. (2017), *A soft robot that navigates its environment through growth*, DOI:10.1126/scirobotics.aan3028.

title: Reproducible multimaterial soft-robot fabrication
open: Manufacture soft robots with predictable geometry, bonding, actuation, and lifetime across batches and laboratories.
status: Integrated multimaterial hands demonstrate promising fabrication; controlling production variation remains necessary for reproducible performance.
why: Moves soft robots from artisanal prototypes toward reliable products.
key_works: Alves et al. (2023), *Integrated Design Fabrication and Control of a Bioinspired Multimaterial Soft Robotic Hand*, DOI:10.34133/cbsystems.0051.

title: Soft-robot design with validated safety–performance tradeoffs
open: Quantify how compliance, speed, payload, and contact geometry jointly affect injury and task performance, then incorporate those measurements into design optimization.
status: Holistic co-design identifies safety and broader design values as unresolved integration issues.
why: Prevents “soft” from being treated as a sufficient safety argument.
key_works: Stölzle et al. (2025/2026), *Soft yet Effective Robots via Holistic Co-Design*, arXiv:2505.03761.

title: Load-bearing self-healing after mechanical damage
open: Restore useful force, sealing, and sensing after puncture or tearing while the robot remains operational, with repeatable healing over multiple damage cycles.
status: Electrical self-healing in HASEL actuators is not equivalent to repairing arbitrary mechanical tears.
why: Makes soft robots viable in abrasive and hazardous environments.
key_works: Acome et al. (2018), *Hydraulically amplified self-healing electrostatic actuators with muscle-like performance*, DOI:10.1126/science.aao6139.

title: Integrated microscale sensing, computation, and motion
open: Integrate useful sensing, state estimation, decision-making, and actuation into mass-manufacturable microscopic robots without external state tracking.
status: Electronically integrated microscopic robots demonstrate semiconductor-compatible fabrication; complete useful autonomy requires additional integration.
why: Enables microscopic systems that do more than follow externally imposed fields.
key_works: Miskin et al. (2020), *Electronically integrated, mass-manufactured, microscopic robots*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-2626-9.

title: Power budgets for autonomous microscopic robots
open: Determine achievable sensing, computation, communication, and locomotion capabilities under realistic microscopic energy supply and heat-dissipation limits.
status: Fabricated microscopic robots establish component feasibility; end-to-end energy allocation remains a fundamental constraint.
why: Identifies physically plausible architectures and impossible specifications.
key_works: Miskin et al. (2020), *Electronically integrated, mass-manufactured, microscopic robots*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-2626-9.

title: Closed-loop navigation in moving biological fluids
open: Navigate microrobots through variable flow and complex boundaries using clinically compatible sensing and actuation, with quantified localization error.
status: Biomedical microrobotics demonstrates many propulsion and guidance approaches; closed-loop operation in realistic anatomy remains demanding.
why: Supports targeted interventions with less invasive access.
key_works: Nelson, Kaliakatsos, and Abbott (2010), *Microrobots for Minimally Invasive Medicine*, DOI:10.1146/annurev-bioeng-010510-103409.

title: Independent control of many field-driven microrobots
open: Control multiple microrobots independently when they share a small number of global magnetic, acoustic, or electric actuation channels.
status: External-field actuation is effective for small devices; shared inputs create controllability and interference constraints.
why: Enables coordinated microscale tasks rather than collective motion alone.
key_works: Sitti et al. (2015), *Biomedical Applications of Untethered Mobile Milli/Microrobots*, DOI:10.1109/JPROC.2014.2385105.

title: Tracking microrobot swarms inside opaque tissue
open: Resolve individual or task-relevant collective states at adequate spatial and temporal resolution without excessive imaging exposure or incompatible instrumentation.
status: Biomedical microrobot reviews identify localization and imaging as essential enabling capabilities.
why: Makes closed-loop therapy and recovery verifiable.
key_works: Sitti et al. (2015), *Biomedical Applications of Untethered Mobile Milli/Microrobots*, DOI:10.1109/JPROC.2014.2385105.

title: Reliable clearance or retrieval after microrobot deployment
open: Demonstrate that deployed devices can be retrieved, safely degraded, or reliably cleared, including worst-case retention and material byproducts.
status: Minimally invasive microrobotics establishes possible interventions; post-task fate is a separate translational requirement.
why: Prevents successful task execution from leaving unacceptable residual risk.
key_works: Nelson et al. (2010), *Microrobots for Minimally Invasive Medicine*, DOI:10.1146/annurev-bioeng-010510-103409.

title: Reproducible biohybrid robot construction
open: Produce biohybrid robots whose morphology and behavior are reproducible across batches despite biological variability.
status: Reconfigurable-organism work demonstrates a design-to-realization pipeline; reliable manufacturing tolerances remain a broader target.
why: Enables meaningful comparison, dependable behavior, and controlled deployment.
key_works: Kriegman et al. (2020), *A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms*, DOI:10.1073/pnas.1910837117.

title: Long-term control of living robotic components
open: Maintain predictable function as living actuators grow, remodel, fatigue, and respond to their environment.
status: Biohybrid and living constructions demonstrate useful behavior; stable long-duration input–output relationships are not automatic.
why: Makes living components usable in engineered systems.
key_works: Kriegman et al. (2020), *A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms*, DOI:10.1073/pnas.1910837117.

title: Year-scale useful underwater autonomy
open: Sustain a defined scientific or inspection mission for a year using available replenishment infrastructure, with bounded intervention and complete maintenance accounting.
status: Long-duration marine platforms exist; combining persistent sensing, manipulation, fouling management, and autonomous servicing remains a stronger integrated target.
why: Enables continuous ocean observation without frequent ship support.
key_works: Yoerger et al. (2021), *A hybrid underwater robot for multidisciplinary investigation of the ocean twilight zone*, DOI:10.1126/scirobotics.abe1901.

title: Underwater localization across changing acoustic conditions
open: Maintain accurate localization when visibility is poor, acoustic propagation changes, and seafloor features are sparse or mobile.
status: Underwater robotic systems combine specialized sensing and navigation; robust operation across simultaneous sensing degradations remains challenging.
why: Supports precise inspection, sampling, and manipulation.
key_works: Khatib et al. (2016), *Ocean One: A Robotic Avatar for Oceanic Discovery*, DOI:10.1109/MRA.2016.2613281.

title: Under-ice exploration with guaranteed return opportunities
open: Explore beneath moving or irregular ice while preserving a defensible route to a recoverable exit despite limited communication and uncertain currents.
status: Ice-world robotic exploration motivates autonomous navigation in confined, hazardous environments; practical return guarantees require explicit environmental assumptions.
why: Makes otherwise inaccessible scientific missions less likely to lose the vehicle.
key_works: Vaquero et al. (2024), *EELS: Autonomous snake-like robot with task and motion planning capabilities for ice world exploration*, DOI:10.1126/scirobotics.adh8332.

title: Dexterous manipulation at extreme ocean pressure
open: Perform precise, force-sensitive manipulation at hadal pressures with durable sensing, actuation, sealing, and pressure-compatible materials.
status: A self-powered soft robot operated in the Mariana Trench; dexterous manipulation at comparable pressure is a substantially richer target.
why: Enables deep-ocean sampling and infrastructure intervention.
key_works: Li et al. (2021), *Self-powered soft robot in the Mariana Trench*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-03153-z.

title: Non-disruptive tracking of fragile marine organisms
open: Follow and observe organisms while bounding disturbance from illumination, sound, flow, heat, and physical proximity.
status: Mesobot was designed for twilight-zone biological investigation; quantitatively proving minimal disturbance across species is a further experimental target.
why: Prevents robotic observation from changing the behavior being studied.
key_works: Yoerger et al. (2021), *A hybrid underwater robot for multidisciplinary investigation of the ocean twilight zone*, DOI:10.1126/scirobotics.abe1901.

title: Coordinated sampling of evolving water parcels
open: Keep multiple robots aligned with a changing water mass while separating biological evolution from transport and sampling bias.
status: Coordinated autonomous Lagrangian microbial studies have been demonstrated; broader spatiotemporal coverage and uncertainty accounting remain open.
why: Enables causal interpretation of ocean biological measurements.
